turns.narration:
You turn toward Saffron and ask whether she has heard the comms static before or seen anyone in a yellow scarf pass through the corridor. She pauses with the wrench against the clamp, then slides out from beneath the fuel manifold and gets to her feet. Grease darkens one cheek; the hangar’s reactor hum fills the beat before she answers.

“Not before today. I saw the scarf pass, but I didn’t get a look at the person.” She wipes her fingers on a rag and returns to the clamp, tightening it with two short turns. The comms speaker gives a dry crackle behind you, while morning light lies in thin bars across the grating.

turns.action: I examine the comms speaker and its wiring, looking for signs of tampering or an
turns.narration:
You crouch beside the comms speaker and trace its cable run along the hangar wall, checking each coupling by touch. The dry crackle cuts in again, rough against the reactor hum. One housing screw sits proud of the others; you loosen it and ease the speaker grille aside.

A thin strand of stripped wire bridges two contacts inside. Its end bears a fresh copper shine, and the insulation around it has started to blacken. You pinch the strand free with your tool. The crackle stops, but the wire snaps in your grip, leaving the short piece useless.

The exposed terminal gives you a clear opening to inspect the rest of the circuit; the interference came from that improvised bridge, not the speaker itself. Saffron looks up from the fuel manifold as you lay the broken strand on the grating, then returns to her work without comment. Somewhere deeper in the hangar, a pressure seal hisses once, and the bare contacts remain inches from your hand.

judge.weakness: The snapped wire and exposed contacts suggest a complication, but neither creates a clear, meaningful cost.

turns.action: I force the pressure-seal hatch open and brace it against the hiss, checking the
turns.narration:
You plant a boot against the grating and wrench the pressure-seal hatch open. The seal breaks with a sharp hiss. Cold air drives through the gap, carrying the bite of ozone across your face as you brace your shoulder against the hatch and peer into the narrow service channel.

A loose pressure line shudders inside the gap, its coupling leaking a thin stream of vapor toward the hangar ductwork. You reach in and clamp the valve shut. The hiss drops to a faint leak, but the hatch jerks under the pressure and slams your bruised leg against the frame. Pain flares; you stagger back, favoring one leg, while the hatch swings half-closed and traps the damaged line beyond your reach.

Saffron drops her wrench and crosses the grating, catching the hatch edge with both hands before it seals. Her jaw sets as the pressure pushes against her arms. The leak has slowed, not stopped, and the cold vapor still threads through the opening between you.

judge.weakness: The narration has the player reach in and clamp the valve, an action beyond what they specified.

turns.action: I look into the service channel and trace the damaged pressure line from the cla
turns.narration:
With Saffron braced against the hatch, you lean into the service channel and follow the damaged pressure line from the clamped valve. The metal edge presses into your ribs; vapor beads cold across your knuckles. You trace the line to a split at the next coupling, just beyond reach from the hatch.

You wedge your tool into the coupling and crank it shut. The leak dwindles to a thin hiss, then stops. The line gives a sharp metallic pop under the strain, and a length of insulation peels away, exposing the pipe beneath. Saffron keeps the hatch open only long enough for you to pull clear, then lets it settle against its frame and returns to the fuel manifold, checking its fasteners with quick, practiced turns.

For a moment the hangar’s reactor hum is the only sound. The exposed pipe glistens with cold moisture, and your ribs ache where the hatch edge pressed them. Somewhere above the starship, a strip light flickers twice.

judge.weakness: Saffron is left bracing the hatch alone, contrary to the player’s stated constraint.

turns.action: I snatch up the bent tool and wedge its kinked tip beneath the stubborn coupling
turns.narration:
You snatch up the bent tool and wedge its kinked tip beneath the stubborn coupling. With both hands, you lever it into place while your forearm holds the fuel line steady. The coupling turns a fraction at a time; the line shifts against your grip, then settles as you seat the joint flush and tighten it down.

Saffron watches your hands, then matches the short, controlled pressure of your heaves, holding the manifold steady. “There,” she says, and checks the joint with a firm thumb. No vapor escapes; the fuel line stays aligned. The bent tool remains usable, its kink pressed flatter beneath the coupling.

A dry crackle cuts through the reactor hum from the comms speaker. Saffron’s hands stop on the manifold. Beyond the hangar mouth, morning light glances off the starship’s patched hull while the static breaks into another brief burst.

judge.weakness: The unexplained comms crackle introduces a new concern after an otherwise clean success.

turns.narration:
You brace the comms speaker against the hangar wall and rip its casing open. The metal cover bends under your hands, then tears free with a brittle snap. Inside, the wiring hangs in a cramped knot. A loose contact taps the housing in uneven beats, feeding the dry crackle through the speaker; your stripped knuckle leaves a bright smear of blood across the casing.

Saffron’s fingers pause on the manifold fastener. She turns her head toward the speaker, then matches the uneven rhythm with two taps against the pipe. When the contact shifts under your touch, her tapping stops. The crackle cuts out, but one ribbon of wiring dangles loose from the opened unit, and the hangar’s reactor hum fills the sudden silence.

You hold the torn casing against the wall while Saffron checks the fuel line, neither of you moving far from the other’s work. The exposed contact rests between your bloodied fingers as the comms speaker stays quiet.

judge.weakness: The narration decides the player continues holding the casing and contact after the stated action.

turns.action: ## I was being cautious, not aggressive
turns.narration:
You brace the already-open comms speaker against the hangar wall and ease the casing wider with two careful fingers. The loose contact sits exposed among the wiring, tapping the housing in uneven beats and feeding the dry crackle through the speaker. You steady the contact; the static thins, then stops. Cold metal presses into your palm, and the speaker’s torn casing hangs crooked from its mount.

Saffron pauses beside the manifold, one hand still resting on the fastener. “Loose contact,” she says. She turns back to the fuel line and resumes checking the joint while you keep the exposed wiring from shifting. Above you, strip lighting hums over the cramped bay; from somewhere behind the starship’s patched hull, three dull knocks carry through the hangar wall.
